subject: Memory problems, move Matt trick eta parameters to model block?

messages.author: 91be17affe770359
messages.subject: Memory problems, move Matt trick eta parameters to model block?
parts:
Hello,
I'm using the Matt trick on a multilevel model. I use the trick at each of three levels (probe, logger, site), for a total of about 130 parameters. I've been writing the trick in the transformed parameters block like this:  
for (i in 1:Nprobe) a_probe[i] <- a_logger[loggerid[i]] + sigma_probe * eta_probe[i];

I'm defining eta_probe in the parameters block. The problem with this is that when sampling, stan keeps track of all the 130 or so etas. This is rapidly consuming memory (I'm repeatedly fitting the model to multiple weeks of data individually using lapply). How can I rewrite this so stan no longer tracks each eta_probe, eta_logger etc.?

I realize I should probably add week as a level to the model, but I'm struggling with how to define that, and I'll save that for another question.


Thanks,
Joey

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Memory problems, move Matt trick eta parameters to model block?
parts:
Declare the transformed parameters in the model block and
also define them there. Then only the parameters are saved.
Of course, you probably want this the other way around, but we
as of yet have no way to define parameters that aren’t output.
It’s on our to-do list.

The other alternative is to prune the output.

A third alternative would be to save whatever you need from
the sample as you create it rather than keeping it all in memory.

- Bob

Thanks Bob,
I have two questions about moving the parameters to the model block.
1) If I move the declaration and assignment of a_probe to the model block, is there a way to save its samples as a generated quantity?
2) I got a warning about incrementing the log probability when I assign from a distribution in the model block. In the manual it says to increment with the log absolute derivative. In this case the Matt trick is equivalent to a_probe ~ N(a_logger, sigma_probe), and there is no transformation of the mean, but there is of the standard deviation. Does that mean I can safely ignore the warning?

Joey

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Memory problems, move Matt trick eta parameters to model block?
parts:
On Feb 20, 2014, at 8:07 PM, Joey Reid <reid...@umn.edu> wrote:

> Thanks Bob,
> I have two questions about moving the parameters to the model block.
> 1) If I move the declaration and assignment of a_probe to the model block, is there a way to save its samples as a generated quantity?

No. You’d have to redefine it as a generated quantity. But that
won’t save any memory on output. If you want to save a variable you
need in th emodel block, define it in the transformed parameters block.

> 2) I got a warning about incrementing the log probability when I assign from a distribution in the model block. In the manual it says to increment with the log absolute derivative. In this case the Matt trick is equivalent to a_probe ~ N(a_logger, sigma_probe), and there is no transformation of the mean, but there is of the standard deviation. Does that mean I can safely ignore the warning?

Yes. We need to tighten up that warning about Jacobians.

What exaclty gave you the warning? It should only show up if
you transfrom the expression on the left of a ~ (or maybe it
got added so it gripes about the first argument of a log-prob function?).

- Bob
>
